frozen_candidate_root_contribution: glm surfaces in the Quran exclusively as one nominal lexeme (sg غُلَام, dual غُلَٰمَيْن, broken pl غِلْمَان) denoting a HUMAN MALE in the young / pre-full-maturity life-stage (a 'boy / youth'). Two features are lexically entailed across all 13 tokens: (1) male sex, and (2) youth bounded above by أَشُدّ (maturity). All richer readings — son/offspring, servant, ward/orphan, merchandise, eschatological servitor, and every moral quality — are supplied by the syntactic frame or context, NOT by the root itself.

internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Every one of the 13 occurrences names a young male person. When the word means 'son' (the 8 annunciation tokens to Abraham, Zechariah, Mary), the sonship is carried entirely by the surrounding frame — نُبَشِّرُكَ بِ (announce to you), أَهَبَ لَكِ (grant to you), يَكُونُ لِى (be mine) — and the reproductive objections (barren wife 19:8, virgin 19:20, old age 3:40) presuppose a male child produced by generation. Strip the frame and only 'young male' remains: unrelated finders simply say هَٰذَا غُلَٰمٌ of Joseph (12:19); Khidr kills an unrelated boy (18:74); the two غلامان are orphans not yet reached أَشُدّ (18:82); the غِلْمَان serve Paradise's dwellers 'belonging to them' (52:24). The single positive age-anchor is 18:82 (يَبْلُغَآ أَشُدَّهُمَا = they had not yet reached maturity), which fixes غلام as the stage BEFORE maturity. That the same noun takes different external adjectives — عَلِيم, حَلِيم, زَكِيّ, plus the name يَحْيَى — proves those qualities are predicated onto a neutral base noun, not part of it.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: NOT kinship/sonship (52:24 servitors belong to the dwellers, not their sons; 12:19 Joseph is not the finders' son; 18:74 an unrelated roadside boy). NOT servant/slave/merchandise (that loading comes from يَطُوف عَلَيْهِم and بِضَاعَة; against it stand the property-owning orphans of 18:82 and the prophet-sons of the annunciation cluster). NOT female (13/13 male). NOT an adult man — bounded above by أَشُدّ (18:82) and contrasted with بَشَر, the mature generative male, in 19:20. NOT morally valenced (ranges over زَكِيّ/عَلِيم/حَلِيم children and the boy killed to forestall طُغْيَان/كُفْر in 18:74/18:80). NO verbal/eventive sense is recoverable: the root is purely nominal, so no 'core action' claim is licensed. Number (sg/dual/pl) is grammatical, not sense-forming.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: At 15:53:6:2 and 51:28:8:2 the ghulam is unborn and carries a mature epithet (aliim 'knowing', reinforced by haliim 'forbearing' at 37:101:2:2), so the youth/age-stage feature is bleached and proleptic here rather than directly demonstrated. It does not overturn the nucleus: the epithet is a separate adjective added precisely because ghulam alone does not supply it, the construction is a bishaarah naming the future boy, and the age feature is hard-anchored below maturity by 18:82 (lam yablughaa ashuddahumaa) with no contradicting token; the word still denotes the category 'boy/youth' even when its referent is future.
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: 'glm = male child / son (a descent-noun)', driven by the numerically dominant annunciation cluster (8 of 13 in the بشّر/وهب/يكون-لي frame), where the son reading is unmistakable. Rejected as primary because it violates the narrowest-account principle and fails at least three tokens: 52:24:3:1 (non-filial servitors), 18:74:5:1 (unrelated boy), 12:19:10:1 (a found commodity, no kin). The 'son' sense is a frame effect of the annunciation/granting verbs acting on the base sense 'young male'; it vanishes the moment the frame is removed (12:19 هَٰذَا غُلَٰمٌ). A single nucleus plus compositional frames covers all 13 with no residue.

internal_discovery.rationale: All three independent lenses (A, B, and adversarial C) converge on the same thin nucleus 'young human male, pre-maturity', and C — running a genuine refutation — could produce no strictly resistant occurrence, only underdetermination of the age feature in the annunciation cluster. Maleness is exceptionless (13/13) and the youth ceiling is explicitly stated (18:82 أَشُدّ), while the two rival enrichments cancel each other: 52:24 defeats any lexicalized 'son', and the unborn-plus-mature-epithet annunciation tokens resist any lexicalized age-criteriality — leaving exactly the thin, edge-bearing nucleus standing. Because the root is exclusively nominal, no verbal core is claimed. The one honestly under-determined variable is the precise UPPER age boundary (18:80 grants moral agency; 52:24 shows able serving), recorded as a bounded rider, not a defeater.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: A male child (to be) whose sonship is frame-supplied by بشّر/وهب/يكون-لي; the noun contributes 'young male', the frame contributes 'offspring of the addressee'.
clusters.classification_rationale: In all 8 the kinship reading is carried by نُبَشِّرُكَ بِ / أَهَبَ لَكِ / يَكُونُ لِى, and the reproductive obstacles (barrenness عاقر 3:40,19:8; old age الكِبَر 3:40,19:8; virginity لم يمسسني بشر 19:20) presuppose a son produced by generation. The distinguishing adjectives (عليم, حليم, زكيّ) and the name يحيى are external predications, proving غلام is a neutral base noun.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 19:20:5:1 contrasts غلام (male child to be produced) with بَشَر (the mature generative male), fixing غلام as pre-adult and male within the very same clause.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: An existing young male encountered in narrative, in dependent/vulnerable status, with no kinship to the interacting party.
clusters.classification_rationale: None is the son of the relevant party: Joseph found and commodified by strangers (12:19 بِضَاعَة), an unrelated boy killed by Khidr (18:74, glossed نَفْس), the same boy with living believing parents feared for طُغْيَان/كُفْر (18:80), and two orphans not yet reached maturity (18:82). This cluster strips the annunciation frame and exposes the bare nucleus 'young male', while 18:82 supplies the decisive age ceiling أَشُدّ.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 18:82:4:2 (أَن يَبْلُغَآ أَشُدَّهُمَا) is the single positive Quran-internal anchor fixing غلام as the life-stage BEFORE maturity. At 18:80:2:2 the ghulam is credited with capacity for tughyan (rebellion) and kufr (disbelief), placing him at the agency-bearing adolescent edge of youth; bounded by 18:82's pre-ashudd anchor this calibrates rather than breaks the youth feature.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Young male attendants who circulate serving the dwellers of Paradise; the serving role and belonging are frame-supplied, the noun contributes 'young male'.
clusters.classification_rationale: Sole broken plural (غِلْمَان), the vowel shift غُلَام→غِلْمَان being morphological number only. The service is predicated by يَطُوف عَلَيْهِم and belonging by لَهُم; imaged as hidden pearls (youthful freshness), confirming the youth+male nucleus with no kinship or inherent servitude in the word itself.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: At 52:24:3:1 the ghilman are servitors 'belonging to' (lahum) the dwellers of Paradise, not their offspring, defeating any lexicalized son/kinship reading of the root.

reconciliation.rationale: The mature quality is adjective-borne, added because غلام does not supply it; the annunciation frame names the future boy (prolepsis), and 18:82's أَشُدّ ceiling keeps the lexical category 'pre-maturity male'. Underdetermination of the age feature here is not refutation.
The adjacent 18:82 غلامان explicitly have not reached أَشُدّ; read together they calibrate the upper edge of youth (childhood through agency-bearing adolescence) rather than breaking the feature.

adversarial_verification.notes: An adversarial pass attacked the nucleus 'young human male, pre-maturity' across all three clusters. Maleness held 13/13 (masculine agreement, son-presupposing objections, no female token). The youth feature is directly anchored by 18:82 (أَشُدّ) and contradicted by no occurrence; the two rival enrichments cancel (52:24 defeats 'son', the unborn-plus-mature-epithet tokens defeat age-criteriality), leaving the thin nucleus with zero failing occurrences. The claim is falsifiable (a female or mature-adult غلام would break it) and distinct from neighbours (kinship terms and بَشَر). The only reservation is bounded underdetermination of the precise upper age limit, which is a strength rider, not a refutation.

independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A build, B build, C adversarial) each arrived at the identical thin nucleus; the adversarial lens explicitly reported that despite deliberate effort it could produce no strictly resistant occurrence.
candidate_root_contribution: glm surfaces in the Quran exclusively as one nominal lexeme (sg غُلَام, dual غُلَٰمَيْن, broken pl غِلْمَان) denoting a HUMAN MALE in the young / pre-full-maturity life-stage (a 'boy / youth'). Two features are lexically entailed across all 13 tokens: (1) male sex, and (2) youth bounded above by أَشُدّ (maturity). All richer readings — son/offspring, servant, ward/orphan, merchandise, eschatological servitor, and every moral quality — are supplied by the syntactic frame or context, NOT by the root itself.

layer_attribution.occurrence_evidence: 13/13 tokens read; all qac_pos=N, qac_verb_form=null; referents male throughout; age ceiling stated at 18:82 (أَشُدّ); non-kin young males at 12:19, 18:74, 52:24; بَشَر contrast at 19:20.
layer_attribution.derivation: One lexeme in one nominal family: sg غُلَام (nom gula`mN, gen gula`mK, acc gula`mFA, def gula`mu), dual غُلَٰمَيْن (gula`mayoni), broken pl غِلْمَان (gilomaAnN); the u→i shift is broken-plural morphology, not a semantic split; no verb/participle/masdar exists.
layer_attribution.lexical_class: A single lexicalized common noun denoting a young human male (pre-maturity); grammatical number is not sense-forming, so the root cannot exhibit multiple unbridged derivational classes.
layer_attribution.contextual_relation: 'Son/offspring' (يكون لي/أهب لك/بشّر بـ), 'servant/merchandise' (يطوف عليهم/بضاعة), 'ward/orphan' (يتيمين), and character (عليم/حليم/زكيّ) are all frame- or context-supplied predications layered onto the base noun, and are held OUT of the root claim as negative boundaries.
layer_attribution.reconciliation: Preliminary resistances at 15:53/51:28 (bleached age) and 18:80 (moral agency) reconcile to CONSISTENT: the mature epithets are external adjectives on a proleptically-named future boy, and 18:80's agency is calibrated by the adjacent pre-أَشُدّ anchor in 18:82; the 'son' competitor is reconciled as a frame effect defeated by 52:24/12:19/18:74.
layer_attribution.unresolved_resistance: No occurrence finally resists the nucleus. The sole open residue is bounded: the precise UPPER age boundary of غلام (mere child vs. agency-bearing adolescent vs. able young servant) is under-determined by 18:80 vs. 52:24 vs. 18:82, and is recorded as a rider rather than a resistant seam.

hard_cases.reason: Sole plural and sole eschatological-servitor use; it kills the strongest rival account ('glm = son/offspring') because these young males belong to and serve the dwellers without being their sons.

evidence_basis.statement: At 52:24:3:1 the ghilman are servitors 'belonging to' (lahum) the dwellers of Paradise, not their offspring, defeating any lexicalized son/kinship reading of the root.

hard_cases.reason: Unborn referent with a mature epithet is the point of maximum pressure on the age-stage feature, showing the youth component is proleptic in the annunciation cluster.

evidence_basis.statement: At 15:53:6:2 and 51:28:8:2 the ghulam is unborn and carries a mature epithet (aliim 'knowing', reinforced by haliim 'forbearing' at 37:101:2:2), so the youth/age-stage feature is bleached and proleptic here rather than directly demonstrated.

hard_cases.reason: Moral-religious agency (طُغْيَان, كُفْر) ascribed to a غلام tests the upper boundary of 'youth'; the one genuinely under-determined variable is the precise ceiling.

evidence_basis.statement: At 18:80:2:2 the ghulam is credited with capacity for tughyan (rebellion) and kufr (disbelief), placing him at the agency-bearing adolescent edge of youth; bounded by 18:82's pre-ashudd anchor this calibrates rather than breaks the youth feature.

hard_case_representation.rationale: No occurrence is finally RESISTANT to the thin nucleus (adversarial lens C produced only underdetermination, not contradiction), so there is no RESISTANT_SEAM. The three ADVERSARIAL_BOUNDARY cases record the strongest disconfirming pressure — 52:24 against the 'son' rival, 15:53/51:28 against age-criteriality, 18:80 against the upper age bound — each with an evidence_basis statement persisted verbatim in a cluster/override note and (for 15:53) in strongest_counterexample.

rejection_condition.challenging_finding: A Quranic occurrence of غ ل م that is unambiguously female, or unambiguously a mature adult male past أَشُدّ, would break the claimed universal nucleus 'young human male, pre-maturity' and force it down to a representative or unresolved scope.
rejection_condition.search_location: All 13 nominal tokens, re-examined for the gender of the referent (pronoun agreement, e.g. فَقَتَلَهُ 18:74, وَأَسَرُّوهُ 12:19) and for any age marker placing a غلام at or beyond أَشُدّ, contrasted against the ceiling in 18:82:4:2 and the بَشَر contrast in 19:20:5:1.
rejection_condition.verification_method: Confirm each referent's sex via morphological agreement and the reproductive-objection frames (عاقر, virginity, old age presuppose a son), and confirm the age ceiling by checking that no token co-occurs with أَشُدّ/completed maturity predicated of the غلام himself.
rejection_condition.confounder_control: Separate frame-supplied meaning (son via يكون لي/أهب لك/بشّر بـ; servitude via يطوف/بضاعة; character via عليم/حليم/زكيّ) from the noun's own content, so that a contextual 'son' or 'servant' is not mistaken for a lexicalized sense and an adjective's adult grade is not read into غلام.
rejection_condition.failure_consequence: If a female or mature-adult غلام is found, downgrade from UNIVERSAL/ROOT_GENERALIZATION to REPRESENTATIVE/LEXICALIZED_CLASS (or UNRESOLVED if the classes cannot be bridged), and retract the maleness or youth entailment accordingly.

reopen_conditions: If a segment-level Arabic alignment or revised morphology reclassifies any غلام token (e.g. 52:24:3:1 غِلْمَان or 18:82:4:2 غُلَٰمَيْن) as something other than the single نoun lexeme, or introduces a verbal/participial form of غ ل م, reopen to test whether a second derivational class exists.

If new analysis fixes the precise upper age boundary now left open by the tension between 18:80:2:2 (agency-bearing: طُغْيَان/كُفْر), 52:24:3:1 (able serving), and 18:82:4:2 (pre-أَشُدّ), reopen to sharpen the youth entailment from 'pre-maturity' to a determinate age band.

If a re-reading of the annunciation cluster (15:53:6:2, 51:28:8:2, 37:101:2:2, 19:19:8:1) is argued to lexicalize غلام as 'son' independent of the يكون-لي/أهب-لك/بشّر-بـ frame, reopen to re-test the single-nucleus verdict against the two-sense competitor.

falsification_evidence.status_rationale: An adversarial pass attacked the nucleus 'young human male, pre-maturity' across all three clusters. Maleness held 13/13 (masculine agreement, son-presupposing objections, no female token). The youth feature is directly anchored by 18:82 (أَشُدّ) and contradicted by no occurrence; the two rival enrichments cancel (52:24 defeats 'son', the unborn-plus-mature-epithet tokens defeat age-criteriality), leaving the thin nucleus with zero failing occurrences. The claim is falsifiable (a female or mature-adult غلام would break it) and distinct from neighbours (kinship terms and بَشَر). The only reservation is bounded underdetermination of the precise upper age limit, which is a strength rider, not a refutation.
